key_insight: An XGBoost model using clinical and ECG features predicted pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) in AV block patients with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction with good discrimination.
clinical_relevance: This could help identify higher-risk patients before or after pacemaker implantation, potentially informing pacing strategy and follow-up intensity.
method: Multicenter prospective RISK-PICM registry analysis of 125 AV block patients with pacemakers
Compared four machine learning models: logistic regression, SVM, random forest, and XGBoost
Used stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter tuning to predict PICM
evidence_signal: PICM occurred in 41 of 125 patients (32.8%) over a median 4.8 years, and XGBoost had the best performance with AUROC 0.831, sensitivity 0.805, and specificity 0.845.
watch_item: The sample was modest and the model needs external validation and workflow testing before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
